record.what_it_does: BigCommerce is an ecommerce SaaS platform whose REST and GraphQL APIs let developers manage store catalog, orders, customers, carts, checkout, content, and more.
record.auth_notes: Store-level and app-level API accounts are created via an OAuth-based flow yielding a stable access_token used in the X-Auth-Token header (not the Authorization header) for most REST/GraphQL Admin endpoints. Legacy Basic-auth API accounts are deprecated and no longer issued to new stores. Some sub-APIs (Storefront GraphQL, Payments) use short-lived Bearer/PAT tokens minted via the main access token; the Tax Provider API uses Basic auth; app lifecycle/customer-login flows use BigCommerce- or user-generated JWTs.
record.access_notes: Developers can sign in to the free BigCommerce Partner Portal and instantly create a Partner Sandbox store (development/testing store, cannot process live transactions) or start a 15-day free trial store, then generate store-level API credentials immediately from Settings > API Accounts in the control panel — no vendor approval step required for dev/test credentials.
record.main_blocker: Production (non-sandbox) use requires a paid BigCommerce store plan, and per-store OAuth app-level credentials require each merchant to install/authorize the app individually

evidence.quote: BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce's REST APIs
Sandbox stores are intended for developing and testing apps. They cannot process any live transactions.
Navigate to the BigCommerce Partner Portal and sign in using your credentials.
The BigCommerce MCP server lets AI agents interact with a BigCommerce storefront using purpose-built commerce tools.
The Catalog API manages products, categories, brands, bulk pricing rules, and more.
BigCommerce publishes downloadable OpenAPI specification files for its REST APIs.
Webhooks notify applications when specific events occur on a BigCommerce store.

record.open_questions: MCP server is beta, storefront-only (guest shopping flow for B2C; B2B coming soon), not an admin/management API MCP — an agent toolkit for store management operations would still need to be built on the REST/GraphQL Admin APIs directly rather than the official MCP.
